methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Aestus Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $10M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company operating in the same sector, including peers such as Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics across Seed through Series B stages.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy anchor, applies a standard 2.0x Series A step-up multiplier to the $10M raised baseline, implying a $20M valuation. Peer-median analysis references a cohort of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.7B, ranging from $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B). The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in funding stage within the peer set.

The two methods produce materially divergent results: stage-progression implies $20M while peer-median implies $1.7B. The triangulated range spans $17M to $2.0B with a median of $860M. The extreme width reflects tension between stage-appropriate valuation mechanics and late-stage peer comparables. Key uncertainties include whether peers' valuations reflect genuine operational milestones or sector exuberance, and whether Aestus's competitive positioning justifies peer-level multiples at Series A. Resolution requires detailed diligence on product validation, unit economics, and market traction.
